text:
### Observed differences

- Six activities became near-universal: in the earlier window, A28, A30 and A31 each appeared in about 97 of 200 traces and A32, A33 and A34 in about 103 of 200; in the later window, all six appeared in about 197–199 of 200 traces. Each occurs at most once per trace in both windows (mean occurrences equal participation; no repetition). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- In the earlier window the six formed two mutually exclusive blocks: A28, A30 and A31 always ran together (in no fixed order among themselves) in the same ~97 traces, A32, A33 and A34 always ran together in the complementary ~103 traces, and no trace contained activities from both blocks (cross-block co-occurrence was 0). In the later window, all six ran in the same trace in about 98 in 100 cases, with the first block before the second in about 98 in 100 cases. [REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027]
- The anchors are stable: A25 preceded and A26 followed whichever block executed, in both windows; in the later window A25 preceded all six activities and A26 followed all six in about 99 in 100 traces. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012]
- Routing changed accordingly: from A25, the share of observed outgoing transitions into A28/A30/A31 rose from about 48% to about 99%, while the share into A32/A33/A34 fell from about 52% to about 1–2%. The direct edges from the first block to A26 disappeared (for example, A28→A26 fell from about 36% to under 1% of A28's observed outgoing transitions), replaced by edges into A32/A33/A34. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
- Event positions shifted modestly: A28/A30/A31 now occur slightly earlier (mean relative position about 0.74 down to about 0.68) and A32/A33/A34 slightly later (about 0.73 up to about 0.77); A25 moved slightly earlier (0.67 to 0.62) and A26 slightly later (0.80 to 0.83). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008]
- Event distances grew where the other block now sits: the gap from A25 to A32/A33/A34 moved from 1–3 positions to 4–5 positions, and the gap from A28/A30/A31 to A26 likewise moved from 1–3 to 4–5 positions. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that two blocks that were previously alternatives are now executed in sequence within the same cases: in the later window, A25 is followed by the block A28–A30–A31 (whose members still run in no fixed order among themselves), which is followed by the block A32–A33–A34 (also internally unordered), with A26 closing the case; in the earlier window, each case contained exactly one of the two blocks after A25, and either block led directly on to A26. [REL015, REL016, REL017, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]

This rests on direct relational evidence — cross-block co-occurrence was 0 before and about 98 in 100 after, always with the first block first — together with the participation rise of all six activities from roughly half of traces to nearly all, and consistent routing, position and distance changes [REL015, REL019, REL022, OCC001, OCC004, DIR001, LAG001, LAG004]. Screening qualified 51 control-flow items where roughly 0.6 would qualify by chance in an unchanged process, so the volume of flags cannot be explained by random sampling as a whole [OCC001–LAG006]. Limitations: the evidence cannot rule out that the two windows contain a different mix of cases (for example, cases that naturally include both blocks becoming more common) rather than a change in routing; it also cannot show whether the choice between the blocks was formally removed. Within-block order remains mixed in both windows, so no fixed sequence inside either block is implied, and the position and distance items use event positions rather than clock time.
